display_title: 皇帝游戏：天下-皇游天下

reviews.text: 这是一款像素风的卡牌肉鸽游戏，卡牌是以麻将为基底，玩家扮演的是皇帝的角色，可填入牌的区域分为文治和武功，文治区填入筒条万，武功区填入东南西北风、红中跟发财。 将手牌中满足条件的麻将牌填入对应的文治区或者武功区，会获得对应的文字和或者武功的政绩点，文治武功政绩点相乘达标即可过关，同时手牌中的麻将牌如果形成胡牌的话，会有额外的分数奖励，这个部分如果对麻将不是规则不是很了解的玩家也可以先不考虑这方面。 这游戏卡牌策略和肉鸽方面主要体现在文臣武将的招募和36计的使用上，因为每一关他可以招募的武文武将是随机的，每个文臣武将拥有自己独特的技能，有的是主动技能有的是被动技能，有的可以当做是麻将牌填入文治武功区，同时招募文臣武将，根据稀有度也是需要花费不同的铜钱，而铜钱是需要根据你每回合所剩的麻将数来统计的，但文臣武将的位置是有限的，超出上限还想招募的话就只能斩掉你已招募的文臣武将，如果斩掉的话，这局游戏中就不会再出现这个文臣武将了，同时每个皇帝自己的技能是不一样的，文臣武将之间和与你所选择的皇帝之间是有羁绊的，如果配合得当，可能会发挥出更好的作用，所以就需要谨慎的考虑，上述这些都是你需要决策的部分，可以见得这个游戏拥有丰富的随机性和需要考验你的决策能力。 最后提几个建议 1.希望能增加Steam成就。 2.希望能清晰的知道每个皇帝的解锁条件。 3.希望制作组能优化完善游戏，减少不知名的卡死bug，不然一个档打半天卡死挺难受的。 4.新手指引方面，我感觉虽然说了一些基础的知道，但稍微复杂点的，比如文臣武将填牌的使用，斩首，胡番型，摧毁牌之类的还是缺乏指引，只能靠自己摸索，希望制作组能加强一下。 5.如果能再增加一下历史人物，历史事件的注解就更好了。 [quote]关注&加入[url=https://store.steampowered.com/curator/32969453/]大众点评[/url]，了解并体验更多好玩游戏[/quote]

皇帝游戏：天下-皇游天下 is a strategy roguelike that blends imperial management, card-based mechanics, and historical Chinese themes into a surprisingly deep and addictive experience. Developed and published by OTTOCOM, the game places players in the role of famous emperors attempting to build stable dynasties while managing ministers, policies, wonders, military affairs, and unpredictable political events. While many strategy roguelikes lean heavily into fantasy settings or abstract mechanics, this game builds its entire identity around Chinese imperial history and legendary historical figures, giving it a distinctive atmosphere that immediately separates it from more generic card battlers. At its core, the gameplay revolves around constructing powerful combinations of ministers, emperor abilities, national policies, wonders, and strategic cards while navigating a constantly changing series of events and challenges. Each run functions similarly to a roguelike deckbuilder, where players gradually assemble stronger synergies and adapt their strategy depending on what characters, upgrades, and events become available. However, instead of focusing purely on combat, the game emphasizes governance and political management just as much as warfare. Economic growth, internal stability, diplomacy, and court management all become important parts of long-term survival, creating a more layered strategic experience than many traditional card-based roguelikes. One of the game’s strongest aspects is how well it uses historical themes within its mechanics. Players can control dozens of emperors inspired by real Chinese dynasties while recruiting famous generals, scholars, ministers, and legendary personalities from history. Certain historical combinations unlock special bond effects and powerful synergies, encouraging players to experiment with different lineups and strategies. Famous alliances and legendary figures are not included simply for decoration; they actively shape gameplay through unique bonuses and interactions. Discovering particularly effective combinations becomes one of the most satisfying parts of the experience because strong political and military synergies can completely transform a struggling empire into a dominant force. The variety of strategic possibilities gives the game excellent replay value. Some runs naturally evolve into militaristic campaigns focused on conquest and expansion, while others reward economic development, cultural influence, or efficient political administration. Randomized events and card offerings constantly force adaptation, preventing players from relying on identical strategies every time. This unpredictability keeps the game engaging across long play sessions because every dynasty develops differently depending on available resources, recruited advisors, and emerging crises. The wonder-building system is another standout feature. Players can construct famous historical projects and infrastructure that provide significant advantages while reinforcing the fantasy of ruling a powerful empire. Building massive wonders not only strengthens gameplay systems but also contributes heavily to the atmosphere of imperial expansion and dynastic ambition. Combined with minister management and strategic policy decisions, the game succeeds at making players feel like rulers shaping the future of a vast kingdom rather than simply controlling cards in isolated battles. One of the most impressive aspects of 皇帝游戏：天下-皇游天下 is the sheer amount of content packed into the experience. Multiple gameplay modes, scenario variations, difficulty settings, and large pools of historical characters ensure that runs remain varied even after many hours. Some modes recreate famous historical periods with alternate outcomes, while others introduce more unpredictable roguelike-style progression systems. Unlockable emperors, advisors, and strategic options create a strong sense of long-term progression that encourages continued experimentation. The game also does a good job of balancing accessibility with complexity, although that balance is not perfect. Early runs introduce players to the basic mechanics gradually enough to understand core systems, but the strategic depth increases dramatically as more features become available. Managing ministers, policies, wonders, resources, military pressure, and event chains simultaneously can become surprisingly intense during later stages. The game constantly demands careful prioritization because poor planning in one area often creates larger problems elsewhere. Visually, the game adopts a clean 2D presentation with anime-inspired character portraits and traditional Chinese influences throughout its interface and artwork. The graphics are not technically advanced, but they remain functional and attractive enough to support the gameplay effectively. Character art gives historical figures personality, while the interface generally communicates important information clearly despite the large number of overlapping mechanics. The soundtrack complements the setting nicely with traditional-inspired music that reinforces the imperial atmosphere without becoming distracting during longer sessions. However, the game is not without flaws. One of the biggest issues is balance inconsistency. Certain combinations of ministers, policies, and abilities are noticeably stronger than others, which can eventually reduce strategic diversity once players begin discovering dominant strategies. Some builds become overwhelmingly effective compared to alternative approaches, making experimentation less rewarding during higher difficulty runs. On the other hand, unlucky early draws or poor event outcomes can occasionally make runs feel unfairly difficult before players have a chance to stabilize their empire. The complexity may also overwhelm new players. There are many interconnected systems operating simultaneously, and the game does not always explain them particularly well. Understanding how various ministers, policy effects, and historical bonds interact requires patience and repeated experimentation. Players unfamiliar with roguelike deckbuilders or historical strategy games may struggle during the early hours while learning the game’s mechanics. Another major limitation is accessibility outside Chinese-speaking audiences. The game relies heavily on text, historical references, and detailed system explanations, yet it currently only supports Simplified Chinese. This language barrier significantly limits its international reach because understanding the mechanics and historical context is essential for fully appreciating the experience. It is unfortunate because the underlying systems are strong enough to appeal to a much broader audience if proper localization support were added. Technical polish is also somewhat uneven. While the game generally functions well, some players have reported interface frustrations, balancing concerns, and occasional bugs during extended sessions. Longer runs can sometimes become slow and mentally exhausting due to the sheer amount of information players must process every turn. Certain late-game sequences feel more cumbersome than strategically exciting because of how many overlapping effects and calculations are happening simultaneously. For fans of strategy games, roguelike deckbuilders, and historical simulations, the game offers an impressive amount of depth and replayability. Its systems can be overwhelming at first, and the language barrier remains a significant obstacle, but players willing to invest time into understanding its mechanics will discover a highly rewarding strategy experience filled with meaningful decisions, powerful synergies, and strong thematic atmosphere. Rating: 8/10

游戏融合麻将和历史元素，亮点与硬伤都十分突出，整体体验喜忧参半。游戏创意值得肯定，将传统麻将玩法与历史人物、羁绊体系相结合，玩法框架颇具新意。剧本模式设计用心，以秦始皇篇章为例，开局会配备李斯、商鞅等历史人物与兵马俑道具，搭配专属组合技，玩法层次感十足，能感受到制作组的构思。卡牌立绘风格统一，古风画风贴合题材，历史角色形象刻画也算用心。 但缺陷同样明显。对局规则限制苛刻，每局仅可出牌三次，不靠技能几乎无法胡牌，上手门槛很高。普通模式没有开局道具与干员加持，难度大幅提升。五虎将这类羁绊效果看似有趣，可干员招募纯随机，很难凑齐触发效果。人物选取违和，郭靖黄蓉这样的武侠角色乱入，却缺失医圣张仲景这类比华佗还厉害的标志性历史人物。 难度曲线严重失衡，普通对局通关本就不易，增幅 200% 的高难度更是劝退多数人。综合来看，玩法创意尚可，但规则与数值打磨不足，更适合愿意钻研玩法的题材爱好者，休闲玩家谨慎入手。
在麻将中融入历史元素，像我这种不熟悉麻将规则的也能轻松入手，玩起来很爽
文治武功就是筹码跟倍数，玩起来有点小丑牌的感觉，有伟业有计策，可玩性还蛮强的
麻将结合帝王肉鸽，胡牌积攒国力闯关，名臣羁绊搭配丰富，单人休闲策略佳作
麻将打牌+帝王武将+小丑牌类肉鸽，玩法新颖独特，构筑上手轻松，一局耗时短，国风趣味十足。缺点是玩法套路单一，内容体量偏小，偏娱乐化，长线游玩容易乏味。适合喜欢小众创意卡牌游戏的玩家。
蛮有意思的一款游戏，就是我不怎么会打麻将但是影响不大，游戏机制蛮多的玩起来蛮有趣蛮爽的
玩皇帝卡牌GMAE，当君主BOSS，麻将版小丑牌，不要小看我和文臣武将的羁绊啊
很好玩的麻将小游戏，加入了各种皇帝对战，很有意思，有点像国风版的小丑牌，不过玩的时候得需要灵活运用技能和删牌，快速找到轮椅才是最优解
本来以为挺复杂，玩两局就差不多知道怎么玩了，搭配武将还挺有意思，武将挺多的，看到熟悉的人物都会想试试能不能配一起
麻将+小丑牌，还能扮演各种古代皇帝，边打麻将还能边治国理政，每个皇帝也有自己不同的特性，玩起来很上头。
游戏的画风挺戳我的，中式麻将的玩法也很不错，创意感拉满，麻将＋小丑牌的组合，越到后期越爽
中式肉鸽麻将牌，创意还是很不错的，特别是每个皇帝都有不同臣子做配合，秦始皇配李斯，后面还有康熙配鳌拜，可玩性和耐玩度都很高啊
游戏不大但挺好玩，招募点文臣武将，排兵布阵，感觉自己真成大佬了。
把麻将玩法和帝王治国融合在一起很有创意，肉鸽随机玩法每一局体验都不一样，像素画风很舒服，玩法很有策略性不枯燥
玩法上的话主要是麻将加小丑牌的肉鸽为主，角色还是很多的，用来杀时间还是非常不错的，越到后面就越爽哦！
《皇游天下》是一款类小丑牌的肉鸽牌组构筑游戏，在这个游戏中，你需要抉择，如何最大效率地打出手中麻将，好让你快速完成每一关的指标，目前来说游戏完成度较低，可游玩的角色较少，看看后续正式版变化如何了。
